title: How Evidence Changes a Public Recommendation: The Riverside Library Late-Hours Pilot
instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，不是官方雅思试题，也不对应任何官方分数。请先听/读英文材料，再完成10道题。听力部分有两位说话人（Maya 和 Daniel），注意他们自然改口和修正的地方。所有题目和选项均为英文；解释为中文。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道新句子的题目。最后完成口语和写作迁移任务。
transcript:
Maya: Okay, Daniel, thanks for coming in early. The library board meets on Thursday, and we still have to decide whether to recommend keeping the late-hours pilot at Riverside branch.
Daniel: Right. So just to recap for the recording — the pilot ran for twelve weeks, from January to March. The branch stayed open until ten p.m. on weekdays instead of eight.
Maya: Yes. And the first report said use went up by about forty percent. That number was in the local paper.
Daniel: It was. But then I looked at the raw counts, and, um — actually the forty percent was only for the first four weeks. After that, attendance dropped. By the last month, evening visits were only about fifteen percent higher than before the pilot.
Maya: So the headline number was real but it didn't last.
Daniel: Exactly. Also, most of the new evening visitors were students from the college across the street. They came for the quiet study room, not for borrowing books.
Maya: Hmm. That matters, because the board's original goal was to help local families who work during the day.
Daniel: Right. And we surveyed those families. Only nine percent said they would use the library after eight p.m. Most said they were too tired or worried about transport home.
Maya: Okay, so the evidence points in a different direction from the first report. What about cost?
Daniel: The extra staff hours cost about 4,200 dollars for the twelve weeks. That's not huge, but it's not nothing.
Maya: And safety? I remember there was an incident.
Daniel: There was one small incident in February — a broken window, probably not related. But the security guard said late evenings were generally calm.
Maya: Good. So my suggestion is this: we don't recommend full late hours for families. Instead, we recommend keeping the study room open until nine for students, and we ask the college to share the cost.
Daniel: I like that. Should we mention the forty percent figure at all?
Maya: We should mention it, but we must explain that it was short-term. If we hide it, people will think we're being selective.
Daniel: Agreed. I'll rewrite the recommendation tonight and send it to you before noon tomorrow.
Maya: Perfect. And let's add one line saying we'll review the numbers again in six months.
Daniel: Done.

grammar.title: 时态、从句、冠词、数量和主谓一致：根据错题复查
grammar.explanation: 先看意思，再看术语。1) 时态：过去发生且已结束用一般过去时（the pilot ran for twelve weeks）；过去某时之前已完成用过去完成时（By the last month, visits had dropped）。2) 从句：宾语从句用陈述语序（I know that the number was real），不要用疑问语序。3) 冠词：特指用 the（the first report），泛指可数名词单数用 a/an（a small incident）。4) 数量：percent 前面用具体数字（forty percent），不可数用 amount of，可数用 number of。5) 主谓一致：主语是单数第三人称，动词加 -s（the report says）；主语是复数，动词用原形（families said）。
grammar.example: the first report said use went up by about forty percent.
